findings.where: Screen 7 (A turn), SHOW text and read
findings.what: "Arrow j starts a quarter turn ahead, so it lands on (−sin θ, cos θ)" skips the step that gets there: no SHOW screen gives the quarter-turn rule (a, b) to (−b, a) applied to (cos θ, sin θ), which appears only in screen 11's Why, so the turn matrix's second column is stated rather than built, against the brief's 'not given as a formula to learn'.

findings.where: Screen 12 (What no matrix does), and screens 1-9
findings.what: The last puzzle tests that a matrix never moves the origin, but no SHOW screen teaches it and it appears only in this puzzle's Why; add one sentence to screen 3 or 5 such as 'The origin is no lots of anything, so it never moves.'

"A mirror such as [−1 0; 0 1] sends i to (−1, 0) and keeps j, so the F faces the other way." is 23 words with two ideas chained, so split it: 'The mirror [−1 0; 0 1] sends i to (−1, 0) and keeps j. So the F faces the other way.'

"Every point is carried this way, so the grid lines stay straight and evenly spaced" skips the reason (each step along a grid line adds the same column) and is unqualified, although screen 9 then squashes the lines together; add the reason and 'unless the move squashes them flat'.

findings.where: Screen 1 (Where i lands), end of the demonstration
findings.what: The settled picture draws the grid and F for [2 0; 1 1] because only i has moved, while the band reads [2 −1; 1 1], so say j waits for the next screen or dim column 2 of the band until screen 2's answer.

The point (2, 1) has the same numbers as column 1, so the Why's '2 lots of (2, 1)' puts the point and the column in one sentence; a point unlike either column, such as (3, 1) landing on (5, 4), keeps them apart.

findings.where: Screen 10 (Which one squashes?), band before Check
findings.what: Before an answer, the band shows the do-nothing matrix [1 0; 0 1] in ink under 'Which matrix squashes the plane onto a line?', so it reads like a fourth candidate; show '?' entries as screen 6 does.

Nothing ties the lesson to Dan's own work: the brief's uses (a turn matrix in a drive's Park transform and the rotating field, a ship's attitude) and the link that the quarter turn (x, y) to (−y, x) is Complex numbers' times j are both missing; one sentence on screen 7 or 11 would cover either.

The analogy says 'use a tape with longer steps' and the breaks then says 'Real tapes share one step size', which contradicts it; and a real up tape can be laid on the other side, so the honest break is that the board itself never deforms, only the marks set out from the tapes.

findings.where: Screen 5 demonstration, about 1.6 s (contact sheet s4)
findings.what: The do-nothing-to-mirror slide passes through flat, and for a moment the closing lines fill the paper with a dense mesh; thin the lines harder near zero or ease through that instant faster.

findings.where: Key under the matrix, 360 px dark (screen 7 moved)
findings.what: The 'start grid' swatch is barely visible against the dark background, so give it the start grid's actual dark-mode stroke at a contrast that reads.
j's arrow is orange, close to the red used for slips, and the brief asked for ink arrows with teal labels, so a darker or non-warm second colour would keep red for mistakes only.
